response.sql: WITH rating_avg AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length FROM film WHERE length IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS base FROM rating_avg), above_baseline AS (SELECT ra.rating, ra.avg_length FROM rating_avg ra CROSS JOIN baseline b WHERE ra.avg_length > b.base), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS kept_avg FROM above_baseline), final AS (SELECT ab.rating, ab.avg_length FROM above_baseline ab CROSS JOIN kept_mean k WHERE ab.avg_length > k.kept_avg) SELECT AVG(f.avg_length) AS mean_avg_length, AVG(f.avg_length - b.base) AS mean_excess_over_baseline, AVG(f.avg_length - k.kept_avg) AS mean_excess_over_kept_mean FROM final f CROSS JOIN baseline b CROSS JOIN kept_mean k;

assumptions.assumption: Rows with NULL length are excluded before averaging, so each rating's average covers only films with a known length; a rating whose lengths are all NULL would be dropped entirely.

The baseline is the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings present in film, and 'kept ratings' in the second step means the set of ratings whose average exceeds the baseline (the 'those ratings' of the request).

'Mean amount by which they exceed' is the average of (rating average minus baseline) and of (rating average minus kept mean) over the final ratings, with no rounding applied. Films with a NULL rating form their own group if any exist; the verified data shows none.
